description: Golden retrieval set for the Northstar AP policy corpus. Three kinds of query, measured separately. 'direct' uses the corpus's own vocabulary and carries the gate. 'paraphrase' asks the same questions in a finance analyst's words, deliberately avoiding the section's terms, because paraphrase recall is the declared weakness of a lexical index and a set that never probes it cannot fail for the reason the retriever actually fails. 'negative' queries are questions this corpus cannot answer. 'accept' lists every section that answers the query; a hit is any of them, and a negative query names none.
notes: Hit@3 and MRR are the operative metrics and cover the direct queries only, so the gated numbers keep their meaning across changes. Hit@1 is reported but not gated: the agent consumes a top-k window, not a single chunk.

Paraphrase recall is reported with its own much lower gate. At the time of writing four of the eight paraphrase queries miss the answering section entirely, which is the measured cost of choosing a lexical index and the number that would justify enabling hybrid retrieval.
The two safety assertions are absolute rather than statistical: the distractor must never appear in a policy result, and the current authority matrix must always outrank the superseded one.

The negative queries also refute a score floor. The highest scoring unanswerable query outscores the lowest scoring answerable one, so no minimum-score cutoff could separate them; the report states both figures.

invoice received but no goods receipt recorded

standard supplier payment terms and when payment runs happen

masking bank details and personal data in application logs
segregation of duties between creating a vendor and approving its invoice
evidence required before posting a month end accrual
applying a credit note against an open invoice for the same vendor
when are two approvals required for a higher risk payment
rounding method and stored inputs for a tolerance calculation
vendor status values that require an invoice to be held
how much can a head of department sign off on their own
